body.statement: Sole headline open obligation (exact two-stage generic strict containment). Execute \(\mathrm{def{:}strictness\text{-}handle}\) on the model \(H=2\), \(S_1=s_0\), \(\mathcal S_2=\mathcal S_3=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), and \(\mathcal R=\{0,1,2\}\). The deliverable is one coefficient-complete algebraic dossier satisfying all of the following requirements: (i) list every rational observed atom \(x_{a_1m_1y_1s_2a_2m_2y_2s_3}\), every rational behavior and oracle-policy probability, the complete affine parameterization \(q=q^0+B\lambda\), and every feasible interval or semialgebraic constraint on \(\lambda\); (ii) display every \(D^{ij}\), every continuation determinant \(G\), every elimination polynomial \(M_j(x,\mu,\pi)\), and one explicit strict sign vector; (iii) prove that the compatible sign region \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{strict}}=\{(x,\mu,\pi):M_j\mathrel{\triangleright_j}0\ \text{ for every listed }j\}\) is nonempty and relatively open, with each relation \(\triangleright_j\in\{>,<,\ne\}\) printed in the dossier; (iv) prove on all of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{strict}}\) that \(\pi_2(\cdot\mid r_1)\) differs for at least two latent rewards and that \(\Delta^-(p)>0\) or \(\Delta^+(p)>0\); (v) give one cell-by-cell exact rational witness, verify normalization, observed marginalization, known behavior factors, positivity, all weak-shadow cross-products, \(A w=\boldsymbol\beta\), the null directions, and certify \(\Theta_I(p)=[229/140,26/15]\) together with exact rational \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) and \(U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) establishing a strict endpoint gap; and (vi) prove that, away from explicitly listed rank-degenerate and reward-history-blind policy faces, the equality locus is exactly the compatible part of the coefficient-expanded common-zero variety \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{eq}}=\mathcal V(M_j:j\in J_{\mathrm{eq}})\), with the index set \(J_{\mathrm{eq}}\) printed. Until this dossier is supplied, generic strict containment is an open question and no existence of the table, sign region, or equality characterization is asserted. Iyengar (2005), Section 2, Theorem 2.1 (finite-horizon robust Bellman equation), p. 261, obtains Bellman recursion after assuming rectangular ambiguity; this obligation must instead establish strict nonrectangularity of an inverse observed-data fiber.
body.justification: A coefficient-complete relatively open strictness region, not the compact-face identity, is the sole theorem-level novelty target.
body.gap: Iyengar (2005), Section 2, Theorem 2.1 (finite-horizon robust Bellman equation), p. 261, assumes a rectangular product of conditional ambiguity sets to obtain robust recursion. Static weak-shadow programs do not determine whether the dynamically coupled inverse observed-data fiber is strictly nonrectangular.
body.consumer: The printed sign certificate would let a sepsis OPE analyst detect when stagewise MNAR bounds are provably too wide for an oracle policy that reacts to latent reward history.

obligation.what_is_open: The coefficient-complete two-stage dossier remains open: no explicit rational observed atom table, affine pair \(q^0+B\lambda\), complete eliminated polynomial family \(M_j\), strict sign vector, exact endpoint calculation, or common-zero index set \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{eq}}\) is present in the frozen core, and this solve does not derive those coefficients.
obligation.obstruction: The compact-face criterion reduces strict containment to emptiness of a simultaneous stage-face system, while the signed-minor calculation only certifies a local objective slope. It does not show that locally forced opposite boundary choices are incompatible with one globally coupled complete-history law. Establishing that incompatibility on a relatively open observable region requires carrying out the specified elimination after choosing and verifying a concrete rational witness; the symbolic handles \(q^0\), \(B\), and \(M_j\) do not themselves contain that calculation.
obligation.attempted: I reduced both endpoint gaps to exact common-face emptiness formulas, parameterized each rank-two \(2\times3\) Chen block by its signed-minor null vector, and computed the continuation slope as \(c^\top z=G\). I also checked that exact CAD decides any fixed instantiated face system. These routes stop before the required cross-stage coefficient expansion and relatively open sign certificate.
obligation.partial_result:
The frozen core does yield the following exact, computable partial characterization.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}compact\text{-}face\text{-}pasting}\),
\[
 \Delta^-(p)>0\iff
 \neg\exists q\left[q\in\mathcal K(p)\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{t=1}^H\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^-(p)\right],
\]
and
\[
 \Delta^+(p)>0\iff
 \neg\exists q\left[q\in\mathcal K(p)\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{t=1}^H\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^+(p)\right].
\]
For a fixed rational or real-algebraic observed law and policies, \(\mathrm{thm{:}fixed\text{-}law\text{-}value\text{-}image}\) makes these emptiness assertions decidable by exact real elimination after the stage endpoints have been computed.

There is also a local observable slope certificate.  For a two-row, three-reward respondent block \(A\), direct cofactor expansion gives
\[
 A(D^{12},-D^{02},D^{01})^\top=0.
\]
If \(A\) has rank two, this vector spans \(\ker A\).  For a continuation coefficient row \(c^\top\), another cofactor expansion gives
\[
 c^\top(D^{12},-D^{02},D^{01})^\top
 =\det[(A_{0\cdot});(A_{1\cdot});c^\top]=G.
\]
Hence, on any feasible line \(w+\lambda z\), the local continuation objective is affine with slope \(G\), and \(G\neq0\) forces a local extremum to a feasibility boundary.  What remains unproved is the global elimination step showing, on one printed relatively open sign region, that the boundary choices forced at the two stages cannot be realized by one common complete-history law.
